solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Divulge receiving phosphorus atom component (6)

indicatorNotes.receiving: LET ON takes P in, as a host receives a guest

blocks.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

annotation.surface: A scientist leaks what happens when phosphorus picks up a particle.
annotation.walkthrough: LET ON splits after LE to take the P. A lepton is a light particle such as the electron.
annotation.definitionFit: Leptons, including electrons, are among the particles that make up an atom.

entries.clue: Source of light wasted, needing measure of current and power introduced (8)

indicatorNotes.introduced: AMP and P are introduced into LOST

blocks.note: the amp is the unit of electric current
P = power, as in physics formulae

annotation.surface: An electrician complains that a wasteful light needs more current and power.
annotation.walkthrough: The electrical words all look like they belong to the definition, but only 'Source of light' does; current and power are building bricks.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the post carries the street lamp, so the whole thing is loosely where the light comes from.

entries.clue: Not entirely weak joke (3)

indicatorNotes.Not entirely: only part of PUNY is used, its last letter dropped

annotation.surface: A comedian's gag falls a little flat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Weak joke' reads as one phrase, but 'weak' is wordplay and 'joke' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun is a joke that plays on a word's two meanings.

entries.clue: Work hard, securing right answer for deprived children (7)

indicatorNotes.securing: to secure is to hold fast, so OP grips the R inside itself

blocks.note: ANS is the usual abbreviation for answer

annotation.surface: Someone toils to find the right solution for poor children.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work hard' reads as one verb, toil, but splits into OP and H.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: the deprivation meant is the loss of parents, not poverty, which the surface suggests.

entries.clue: Former student tired having gone round front of college block (8)

indicatorNotes.having gone round: to go round something is to encircle it, so STALE wraps the C

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil
a tired joke is a stale one

annotation.surface: A weary graduate wanders round a college building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'College block' looks like a building, but block is the definition in its sense of hindrance.
annotation.definitionFit: An obstacle is something that blocks the way.

entries.clue: Something to help EV driver, finally, after accusation of assault? (7,7)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of driver
indicatorNotes.after: the R comes after BATTERY CHARGE

blocks.note: being accused of assault and battery is facing a battery charge

annotation.surface: An electric-car driver ends up accused of assault.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition stops at EV (electric vehicle); 'driver' is only there for its last letter, though it seems to finish the phrase 'EV driver'.
annotation.definitionFit: An electric vehicle runs on a battery, and a battery charger tops it up.

entries.clue: Conflicted about love, is upset in wrench (7)

indicatorNotes.about: TORN goes round the other pieces
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down answer, upset turns IS upside down to SI

annotation.surface: Someone torn over a love affair is thrown into turmoil.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pretends 'wrench' is emotional, but it is the twisting force on a spanner-turned bolt.
annotation.definitionFit: Torsion is twisting, and to wrench is to twist forcibly.
annotation.definitionNote: wrench is a noun here: a twisting pull

entries.clue: Study more than half of traffic — minimum levels in set-ups around roadworks (11)

indicatorNotes.more than half of: four of the seven letters of traffic are kept

blocks.note: to con is to study closely
lows = minimum levels, as in record lows

annotation.surface: A report studies traffic slowing to a crawl near roadworks.
annotation.walkthrough: A contraflow is the British arrangement where traffic is moved onto the opposite carriageway to pass roadworks.
annotation.definitionFit: Contraflows are traffic arrangements set up to get vehicles round roadworks.

entries.clue: Catch new music, say, turning up in recording (6)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down answer ART reads upwards as TRA
indicatorNotes.in: 'in recording' places the new music inside the record, so N and TRA sit within EP

blocks.note: music is an example of ART, turned up

annotation.surface: A fan tries to catch some new music appearing on a record.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks music as one example of ART rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually of catching someone out by a trick.

entries.clue: Loin meat cleric misrepresented as spam etc (10,4)

indicatorNotes.misrepresented: the letters are presented wrongly, rearranged

annotation.surface: Loin meat passed off as Spam, the tinned pork, with a clergyman involved.
annotation.walkthrough: Spam the tinned meat sits comfortably beside loin meat, but here spam is junk messages.
annotation.definitionFit: Spam and similar messages arrive by electronic mail.

entries.clue: Chap turned up in clutches of fidgety tailor, one busy with their hands? (11)

indicatorNotes.turned: a thing turned round faces the other way, so UP reads backwards as PU
indicatorNotes.in clutches of: PU sits inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: TAILOR rearranged, split to hold PU

annotation.surface: A man gets caught up with a nervous tailor who never stops handling things.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: manipulate comes from Latin manus, hand, so a manipulator literally works with the hands.
annotation.definitionFit: A manipulator handles things, whether objects or people.

entries.clue: New opponent in game, one easily confused? (3)

blocks.note: in tag, whoever is 'it' chases everyone else

annotation.surface: A new rival in a game is baffled.
annotation.walkthrough: In British usage a nit is a dim person, a nitwit; the question mark admits that the definition is loose.
annotation.definitionFit: A British colloquial sense: short for nitwit, a dimwit, and the question mark owns up to describing rather than defining.

entries.clue: Expert’s account defending India is unimaginative (7)

blocks.note: India is I in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A consultant's report on India is judged dull.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S is used as letters: PRO'S gives PROS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: prosaic began as 'like prose' and came to mean dull and matter-of-fact.

entries.clue: Historic corruption? Creative interpretation of events dismissing pressure (8,3)

indicatorNotes.dismissing: P is sent out of ORIGINAL SPIN

blocks.note: a new slant, an original spin, on events

annotation.surface: Press officers spin a scandal from long ago without applying pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: Original sin is the corruption inherited from Adam's fall; 'historic' with a question mark stretches that to the first sin in history.
annotation.definitionFit: Original sin is the inherited moral corruption dating from the Fall.

entries.clue: Country’s anger reflected curtailment of party, perhaps (7)

indicatorNotes.reflected: IRE reads back to front, as in a mirror
indicatorNotes.curtailment of: curtail literally means cut the tail, so TREAT loses its last letter

blocks.note: a party is one kind of TREAT, cut short

annotation.surface: A nation's fury is mirrored in the cancelling of a festivity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country's' needs the 's read as 'is': Country is anger reflected plus the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Horn of Africa state is one example of a country.

entries.clue: Versatile tool, swanky, misfires when deployed (5,4,5)

indicatorNotes.when deployed: the letters are spread out and rearranged

annotation.surface: A flashy gadget keeps failing whenever it is put to use.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a sneer at a posh gizmo; nothing in it points to Switzerland.
annotation.definitionFit: A Swiss Army knife folds many tools into one handle.

entries.clue: A lot of publicity and a lot of attention may be mesmerising (8)

indicatorNotes.A lot of: most of HYPE: drop the last letter
indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of NOTICE: drop the last letter

annotation.surface: Heavy press coverage and public attention can hold people spellbound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' reads as quantity, but here it is a trimming instruction: most of the word, not much of the thing.
annotation.definitionFit: Hypnotic means mesmerising, holding the attention as if in a trance.

entries.clue: Exaggerate problems in column, supported by two articles, and leave city (4,2,3,5)

indicatorNotes.supported by: the articles follow on after PILE ON
indicatorNotes.and: adds GO and NY at the end

blocks.note: a pile is a column driven into the ground to support a building
on = in, as in 'on the team'

annotation.surface: A columnist, backed by a couple of pieces, overstates the city's woes and quits town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Problems in column' reads like newspaper troubles, but 'problems' closes the definition and 'in column' is wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: To pile on the agony is to make a situation sound worse than it is.

entries.clue: Authorise it during tender, $1000 being expended (7)

indicatorNotes.during: something happening during another is within its span, so IT sits inside the word
indicatorNotes.being expended: money expended is spent and gone, so the G leaves GENTLE

blocks.note: G = grand, a thousand dollars; removed

annotation.surface: Someone approves a bid in which a thousand dollars is spent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tender' tempts as a bid, which fits the money; it is actually the adjective, GENTLE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean granting someone a right to do or have something.

entries.clue: Tech company in the vicinity of Cumbrian town (7)

blocks.note: Apple, the maker of the iPhone

annotation.surface: A technology firm sets up near a small town in the English Lakes.
annotation.walkthrough: Appleby-in-Westmorland is a market town in Cumbria, in north-west England, known for its horse fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a place name clued by its county, Cumbria in north-west England.

entries.clue: What physio may apply before reserve comes off? (3,3)

annotation.definition: What physio may apply before reserve comes off?

blocks.note: read straight, the treatment a physio puts on an injury: a bag of ice
a player's name ahead of the reserve's reads as ICE then BAG, since to bag is to reserve (bag a seat)

annotation.surface: A physiotherapist treats a player before the substitute leaves the field.
annotation.walkthrough: The sports surface hides a second reading: ICE is what a physio applies, and it comes before BAG, to reserve, as in bagging a seat.
annotation.definitionFit: An ice bag is a bag of ice put on an injury to reduce swelling.

entries.clue: Confused bloke clipped on the ear (7)

indicatorNotes.clipped: to clip is to trim a little off, so CHAP loses its last letter

blocks.note: CHAP = bloke, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A dazed man has been cuffed round the head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clipped on the ear' is a British phrase for a light slap; here clipped trims CHAP and 'on the ear' becomes OTIC.
annotation.definitionFit: Chaotic means in total disorder, confused.

entries.clue: Persuades Earl to invest in reform of prison (5,2)

indicatorNotes.to invest in: E is placed inside, as money is invested in
indicatorNotes.reform of: PRISON is re-formed into new letters

annotation.surface: Someone lobbies a nobleman to put money into prison reform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invest in' reads as finance, but here it only means put inside.
annotation.definitionFit: To rope someone in is to persuade them to take part.

entries.clue: America getting behind baseball’s foremost coach? (3)

indicatorNotes.getting behind: in an across answer, behind means later in the line, so US follows the B
indicatorNotes.foremost: the foremost part of a word is its front, its first letter

annotation.surface: The USA rallies behind its leading baseball trainer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a sports trainer after baseball; the question mark hints at the other coach, a road vehicle.
annotation.definitionFit: In Britain a coach is a long-distance bus.

entries.clue: Setter cared about proprietary information (5,6)

annotation.surface: The crossword setter was worried about protecting confidential details.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts you to write in ME or I, but here it is just letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A trade secret is information a business keeps to itself as its own property.

entries.clue: Rent ready for reduction (3)

indicatorNotes.for reduction: RIPE is reduced by its last letter

blocks.note: RIPE = ready (of fruit), minus the E

annotation.surface: Rent that is due to be lowered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is the noun for a tear.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, using the less common noun sense of rent: a tear, from the verb rend.

entries.clue: Taking extreme care with lady’s clothing after spicy stuff (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is an adverb; the definition is a phrase describing how something is done

indicatorNotes.clothing: the outside of lady, its clothes, is used
indicatorNotes.after: after means coming later in the line, so the lady's clothing follows GINGER

annotation.surface: A cook handles the hot spices very carefully while dressing a woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lady's clothing' hints at dresses; it means the letters that clothe LADY, its outside.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose gloss: gingerly describes the cautious, delicate way something is handled.

entries.clue: Nothing in photo I took, seeing only what’s close (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'nothing in photo' puts the zero within the picture's letters

blocks.note: a photo I took is my pic

annotation.surface: A photographer admits the snapshot came out blank, being short-sighted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Photo I took' is a paraphrase to be turned into first-person slang, the possessive plus the short word for picture.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone myopic is short-sighted, seeing clearly only what is near.
